1. Collective action can enable farmers to access high value markets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how collective action can help smallholder farmers to access higher value market outlets.
the role of social capital in enabling smallholder farmers to meet the requirements of higher value markets and to sustain linkages with these markets.

how collective action can be used as a tool for smallholder farmers in developing countries to improve their livelihoods by linking them into higher value markets and how collective action can help to sustain those linkages over time.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the farmers' collective action and market led learning approach enabled the farmers to sustain their linkages to the market and to increase their incomes.
the group was able to sustain the market linkage to the fast food chain because it had a strong and committed leadership and the group members were willing to learn new skills and adopt innovations.
the farmers' group in question has demonstrated that it is possible to sustain sales to a modern food outlet in Uganda, provided the group has the capacity to learn and the willingness to change.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the farmers' association was able to meet the challenges of upgrading and sustaining links to the fast food outlet through collective action and a learning process that combined technical, organizational and marketing innovations.

the group was able to meet all the requirements of the market, but that the group was not able to achieve the full potential of the market because of a lack of capacity and a lack of market information.
the farmers' group has been successful in sustaining linkages to a modern food outlet through collective action.
The main takeaway from our work is that
collective action is not a panacea for all the problems facing smallholder farmers in Africa.
smallholder farmers are capable of meeting the quality standards required to supply high value markets.

collective action is an important tool for farmers to access and maintain links to high value markets, and that market led learning is an effective approach to building farmers' skills, knowledge, social capital and business management capacity to meet the demands of high value markets.
